Two Gamma RV objects have equal classes exactly when their lifts have equal classes.

The converse lifts Gamma RV isomorphisms by the Gamma-definable prescribed-volume lift (special-transformations Gamma 9.16, whose new step bounds the rank of points of Gamma sets by their RV dimension) and Gamma elementary blowups by Gamma charts. The semiring laws are the actual relabelling isomorphisms, which act by coordinate selections and are therefore Gamma. Transport the structure along Proposition 7.9.

The linear form over the Gamma-named semiring is deferred.
proof: Gamma head integrals descend to almost-everywhere classes through generic Gamma witnesses; head Fubini compares appended Gamma standard objects; coordinate permutations are Gamma Jacobian transforms. Additivity of the head integral cuts the head preparation of a sum along the summand tag and compares each cut with its summand at generic points.

title: Gamma-named function module and linear integral
section: Section 7: supported functions and integral identities
statement: Gamma-named RV classes of every degree act on the graded Gamma-named almost-everywhere functions (weighted degree zero and every positive coefficient degree) by coefficient-first actual products. The action is biadditive, unital and associative, so the graded functions form a module over the Gamma-named RV semiring, and the graded Gamma-named integral is linear over that semiring.
proof: At every VF point the row of a product is the actual product of the row coefficient with the row, so the module laws are the product laws of Gamma RV classes in the row contexts. For the integral, the appended full lift of a coefficient product is Gamma isomorphic to the product of the coefficient lift with the appended full lift, Gamma standard contractions of products and of weighted degree-zero factors are products of contractions, and Gamma VF permutation covariance identifies the appended convention.

title: Gamma-named linear Proposition 7.12
section: Section 7: supported functions and integral identities
statement: Gamma Jacobian transforms commute with Gamma-named coefficients of every degree on functions of every degree, almost everywhere. Graded Gamma-named functions supported in a Gamma VF set form a module over the Gamma-named RV semiring, the Jacobian transform of a Gamma VF bijection is linear, and the supported integral over the target composed with the Jacobian transform equals the supported integral over the source, as linear maps.
proof: Two Gamma Jacobian value maps give almost-everywhere equal transforms. For a coefficient product, the Jacobian value of the factor composed with the projection is a Jacobian value of the product, and the rows of the resulting transform are the coefficient products of the rows. Linearity then reduces the identity to the homogeneous Gamma-named 7.12 on each component.

title: Gamma-named normalized Theorem 7.15
section: Section 7: supported functions and integral identities
statement: The Gamma-named degree-one point class is central in the Gamma-named RV semiring; localizing at it and normalizing homogeneous terms gives the Gamma-named normalized coefficient ring. On normalized supported functions (the scalar extension of the supported module), the normalized integral over the target composed with the normalized Jacobian transform equals the normalized integral over the source.
proof: The point commutes with positive classes by the Gamma-definable unsigned swap in lower RV dimension, and with weighted degree-zero classes by the Gamma mixed swap. The normalized maps are the scalar extensions of the linear maps of linear 7.12, so the identity follows on generators from linear 7.12 and the universal property.

title: Gamma-named head-integral coefficient linearity
section: Section 7: supported functions and integral identities
statement: Head integrals of Gamma-named functions commute with Gamma-named coefficients almost everywhere, for positive and weighted degree-zero coefficients on positive and weighted degree-zero functions. Consequently the graded head integral is linear over the Gamma-named RV semiring, raising the component index by one, and the graded integral is invariant under it.
proof: At a VF point the row of a head integral is the contraction of the unary head-fibre family. For a coefficient product, a Gamma native presentation of the coefficient over the VF field base of the row admits a Gamma unary special preparation, so the coefficient-times-fibre family has a Gamma standard contraction that is the coefficient product of the fibre contraction. The two contractions are compared by the Gamma Lemma 7.5 for families at every point, or, in the weighted degree-zero cases, at generic points over frozen generated contexts, and rows at generic points determine almost-everywhere classes.

title: Gamma-named linear Proposition 7.11 and Theorem 7.14
section: Section 7: supported functions and integral identities
statement: The graded Gamma-named coordinate integral along a VF coordinate projection is linear over the Gamma-named RV semiring and agrees with the additive coordinate integrals on each component. The graded integral over the retained coordinates composed with it is the graded integral, as linear maps; hence two nonempty retained coordinate sets give the same iterated integral. The statements concern all graded Gamma-named functions on the full VF space.
proof: Graded functions supported in the full VF space are all graded functions, so a coordinate permutation is the linear Jacobian transform of the permutation bijection and preserves the integral by linear 7.12. Prefix integrals are iterated graded head integrals and preserve the integral by graded head Fubini. The coordinate integral is the composite of a reindexing, the permutation and a prefix integral.

title: Gamma-named normalized Theorem 7.14
section: Section 7: supported functions and integral identities
statement: On normalized Gamma-named functions on the full VF space, the normalized integral over the retained coordinates composed with the normalized coordinate integral is the normalized integral; for two nonempty retained coordinate sets the normalized iterated integrals agree.
proof: The normalized coordinate integral and the normalized integral are the scalar extensions of the linear graded maps along the normalization map, so the identity follows on generators from linear 7.11 and the universal property.
